## Context / Problem
The READ-ONLY, S3-backed live **Jira Cloud** multi-project bridge rehearsal was
dropped when the effort pivoted to Jira Data Center. Sibling story 368f landed the
DC harness (git/file-backed, throwaway low-volume projects). Two dimensions DC
cannot exercise remain uncovered: the **S3 store backend** and **real Cloud ticket
volume/diversity** across the two real Cloud projects **REB** and **DIG**. This
story restores that coverage — strictly read-only against Cloud.

## Approach
Add a new opt-in live suite `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/` that drives the
reconciler against REB + DIG over an ISOLATED, S3-backed copy of the ticket store,
using ONLY read paths proven non-mutating on Jira:
- **Inbound fetch** via `rebar_reconciler.fetcher.compute_snapshot(...)` — the
  read-only counterpart of `fetch_snapshot` (writes nothing; only issues JQL
  searches). The store's `projects.json` mapping drives a per-project JQL fan-out
  (`fetcher._build_snapshot`), so a REB+DIG mapping fetches both projects.
- **`rebar.bridge_preview(...)`** — dry-run (`Mode.DRY_RUN` → `MODE_CAPS=0` →
  `persist=False`), so no leaf applier runs and nothing is written to Jira or the
  store.
Structural read-only enforcement: an autouse fixture monkeypatches every mutating
method on the Cloud transport class (`AcliClient.create_issue/update_issue/
add_comment/add_label/remove_label/set_entity_property/delete_issue/
transition_issue_by_name/unassign_issue/set_parent/update_priority/
update_issuetype/update_comment/delete_comment/delete_issue_link`) to raise, so the
suite is STRUCTURALLY unable to invoke an outbound Jira mutation; read methods are
untouched. Every Jira-touching scenario also asserts per-project issue counts are
identical before and after (belt-and-braces).
The store is a FRESH, isolated store (never the production remote): its ONLY git
remote is a throwaway `s3://<bucket>/<unique-prefix>` wired via `git-remote-s3`,
with `REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off`. Store CONTENT is irrelevant to a read-only fetch (volume
comes from live Jira), so a minimal store is the correct, lighter isolation
boundary — it cannot reach production. The prefix is deleted in teardown.
Avoiding the prior failure: map ONLY real, reachable projects (REB, DIG). One
negative-control scenario maps an UNKNOWN key and asserts the fetch FAILS CLOSED
(raises), never silently succeeds — the documented correct behaviour.

## Scope
- `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/conftest.py` (new) — gating sentinel
  `_live_jira_ready` (earns `jira_live`), the isolated S3 store fixture, the
  structural read-only guard fixture, and the throwaway-prefix teardown.
- `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/test_multi_project_rehearsal.py` (new) — the
  read-only scenarios below.
- `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/README.md` (new) — runbook + env vars.
- `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml` (edit) — a new manually-dispatched
  `jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal` job running `pytest -m external
  tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3 -q -rA`, plus `--ignore=tests/external/
  live_jira_cloud_s3` on the existing `external` job so it is not double-collected.
This is a test/CI-only change; no `src/rebar` runtime code changes.

## Testing
This ticket IS a live test suite. Scenarios (all read-only):
1. `test_one_store_maps_both_projects` — the S3 store maps REB and DIG with the
   expected repo lists; its only remote is the throwaway S3 prefix.
2. `test_inbound_fetch_pulls_both_projects` — `compute_snapshot` with REB+DIG mapped
   yields keys from BOTH projects at real volume (each project > 0; total in the
   thousands), every key ∈ {REB,DIG} (per-project attribution via key prefix).
3. `test_fetch_is_scoped_per_project` — REB-only mapping → snapshot ⊆ REB and zero
   DIG; DIG-only → ⊆ DIG and zero REB (mapping scopes the fetch; no contamination).
4. `test_bridge_preview_read_only_and_scoped` — `bridge_preview` plan targets only
   REB/DIG; per-project Jira counts identical before/after.
5. `test_s3_store_roundtrips_with_mapping_intact` — push the store's `tickets`
   branch to the S3 prefix, clone it back, assert the REB+DIG mapping survives.
6. `test_unknown_project_fails_closed` — an unknown mapped key makes `compute_snapshot`
   RAISE (fail-closed), never a silent empty fetch.
7. `test_read_only_guard_is_real` — calling a patched mutator raises, proving the
   structural guard is not vacuous.
Local validation: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` on the new files;
`pytest --collect-only`; then a real green `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1 pytest -m external
tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3 -q -rA` against live REB+DIG+S3.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The new suite exists under `tests/external/live_jira_cloud_s3/`, is gated by
      `REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL` + Jira/AWS creds, and enforces the read-only invariant
      STRUCTURALLY (verified: `test_read_only_guard_is_real` passes and the guard
      fixture is autouse on every Jira-touching test).
- [ ] It is wired into CI as a dedicated `jira-cloud-s3-rehearsal` job in
      `.github/workflows/external-integration.yml`, and the `external` job ignores
      the new dir (verified by reading the workflow).
- [ ] An ACTUAL green live run demonstrates all five validations — both projects
      fetched into one S3 store, correct per-project resolution, read-only preview
      scoping, S3 round-trip, and ZERO Jira writes (verified: the captured
      `-rA` run output is attached as a ticket comment, showing before/after Jira
      counts equal and the guard active).
- [ ] The throwaway S3 prefix is deleted after the run (verified: an `aws s3 ls`
      of the prefix returns empty, recorded on the ticket).
- [ ] `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `mypy` pass on the new files.
